div.head: III Em 3
div.ab: [III.] Et nolo, ut aliquis recipiat alterius hominem, priusquam quietus sit erga omnem manum, que rectum querat ab eo; et qui aliquem manutenebit et firmabit ad dampnum faciendum, custodiat, ut representet eum ad emendandum, uel ipse componat quod alius componere debebat.

Et nolo ut aliquis recipiat alterius hominem, priusquam quietus sit erga omnem manum quae rectum quaerat ab eo; et qui aliquem manutenebit et firmabit ad dampnum faciendum, custodiat, ut repraesentet eum ad emendandum, vel ipse componat quod alius componere debebat.

And it is my will that no-one receive [into his service] one who has been in the service of another man, until he be quit [of all charges preferred against him] from any quarter where justice is sought from him; and he who shall support and harbour anyone who perpetrates crime shall see to it that he bring him to make compensation, or shall himself pay what is due from the other.
div.note: Some of Liebermann’s notes here are cut off in the gutter of the scan used, and are still to be completed.
Latin only; no German translation in Liebermann.

note.seg: ⁊ ic nylle, þæt nan man underfó oðres mannes man, ær he sy laðleas wið ælce hand las Or. laut II Ew 7. I As 4
⁊ ic nylle, þæt nan man underfó oðres mannes man, ær he sy laðleas wið ælce hand was the reading of the original, according to II Ew 7. I As 4

seþe to þam hearme geheold ⁊ feormie, warie (?) þæt he hine læde (oder gebrenge?) to bote, oððe he sylf bete (oder forgielde) þæt se oðer betan sceolde las Or. laut I Eg 6. II As 3. II Cn 33. (Hl 15) Hu 7, 1. III Eg 6, 1. II Atr 9, 2. Vgl. Gl Haftung 7d

seþe to þam hearme geheold ⁊ feormie, warie (?) þæt he hine læde (or gebrenge?) to bote, oððe he sylf bete (or forgielde) þæt se oðer betan sceolde was the reading of the original, according to I Eg 6. II As 3. II Cn 33. (Hl 15) Hu 7, 1. III Eg 6, 1. II Atr 9, 2. Cf. Gl Haftung 7d
Liebermann suggests that the A.S. text read se þe to þam hearme geheold ⁊ feormie, cf. I Edg. 6.

Liebermann suggests warie (?) þæt he hine læde etc. as the reading of the original A.S. text, i.e. ‘take heed that he bring him’ etc. Such a use of custodire with ut or ne is frequent in post-Augustan prose, and for warian used intransitively or reflexively with the same sense see BT. p. 1169, s.v. i, ii b and cf. II Atr. 9, 1.
